transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Horizon Channel), Maya Gomez (Horizon SA), Ethan Brooks (Horizon Sales)

Summary: quick pipeline review for co-sell motions; align on top accounts, technical gating (VPC/private, SOC 2, SSO), pricing anchors, and next steps to run joint benchmarks.

00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time today, do we have everything on the calendar?
00:06 Jordan Patel: Yep, all good. Thanks Alex. We wanted to make sure we lined up the top deals and then talk through enablement
00:15 Alex Chen: Great. Priya, do you want to kick off with the quick technical checklist?
00:20 Priya Nair: Yeah sure. Quick note, I'll be a little granular. For the accounts you flagged, the main technical gating we've seen is private deployment or V P C peering, and also K M S integration for keys - sometimes customers ask for H S M. I want to confirm Horizon is okay with us showing both hosted and dedicated options in the co-sell pitch?
00:38 Jordan Patel: Absolutely. Most of our targets are enterprise telco and finserv where either dedicated or private are table stakes. We want the rep to be able to say both are supported.
00:46 Maya Gomez: On the security side we need to make sure SOC 2 Type II and ISO stuff is clear, and we also have a couple customers who ask for explicit E U data residency. Can Redwood provide an EU region SLA?
01:05 Priya Nair: We do. We have EU regions in our Dedicated and Hosted catalog; SLA depends on Dedicated commitments. I'll follow up with the exact SLA language.
01:14 Alex Chen: Cool. High level agenda: pipeline review (who's in which stage), pricing anchors, tech blockers, enablement materials, and then next steps. Jordan, can you run through the top eight accounts you mentioned earlier?
01:26 Jordan Patel: Sure. Quick list: 1) NovaBank - POC requested, 2) Meridian Communications - evaluation, 3) Orbis Health - procurement review, 4) SummitEdge - budget approval, 5) Vertex Logistics - technical deep dive set, 6) SkyLine Systems - legal loop, 7) LumenWorks - interested in private deployment, 8) QuantifyCo - exploring proofs. I'll put the sheet in the shared drive after this.
01:49 Ethan Brooks: For NovaBank they're specifically asking about latency SLOs for sub-200ms on gen workloads, and cost per 1k tokens. They want to see a baseline against Anthropic and OpenAI.
02:06 Priya Nair: (laugh) small correction - timestamp jumble but yes - we can run bench. For NovaBank we recommend the Dedicated config with 8xA100 equiv or the quantized variant to hit cost targets. We'll need about two weeks to run the baseline and we can show both hosted vs dedicated economics.
02:30 Jordan Patel: What's the ask from Horizon sales enablement side? Do you want a joint one-pager, or a full deck?
02:38 Alex Chen: Both. A joint one-pager that reps can use in discovery, and a co-sell deck for executive meetings. Also a battlecard that covers objections (latency vs cost, data residency, SLA differences). We'll share a template of the co-sell slide and the partner pricing sheet.
03:00 Maya Gomez: On compliance docs, we have a standard security questionnaire we send to customers. We'll need Redwood's SOC 2 report and some answers about encryption at rest, token retention, and audit logs. Can you drop those into the shared folder?
03:16 Priya Nair: Yes, we'll send SOC 2 and a short FAQ about retention and K M S. Note: sometimes the transcriptions of product names get butchered - our docs will be the source of truth.
03:28 Jordan Patel: Pricing is always the sticky point. We need partner pricing that allows Horizon to have a co-sell discount and also room for the reseller margin. Can you propose a partner discount schedule?
03:41 Alex Chen: We'll propose a tiered partner pricing: small deals - standard hosted discounts; mid-sized - Dedicated commit discount; strategic - custom. I'll add recommended margin bands in the pricing sheet.
03:52 Ethan Brooks: For Meridian Communications they want a POC that integrates with their existing Kafka-based ingestion. Are there known connectors?
04:00 Priya Nair: We don't ship a turnkey Kafka connector out of the box but we have reference integrations and sample code. We can scope a POC that uses a lightweight adapter; takes a few days to stand up. We'll include that in the POC plan.
04:20 Jordan Patel: Good. For Orbis Health, data residency + HIPAA concerns will push them to Private deployment; will Redwood's Private on-prem option be feasible?
04:32 Priya Nair: Yes, Private can be deployed on-prem or VPC with a private control plane; we have customers doing that. There is an onboarding window though - typically 6-8 weeks for full on-prem. If Orbis wants a quicker path, a dedicated VPC in their cloud region is faster.
04:56 Maya Gomez: For LumenWorks, they asked about quantization - will that change quality vs the customer's accuracy thresholds?
05:04 Priya Nair: It can. We'll recommend running evals on the customer's prompt set. Redwood Optimize gives suggestions and model/quantization recommendations by workload — we'll include an eval plan in the benchmark scope.
05:22 Alex Chen: Let's talk ownership on joint outreach. Jordan, you mentioned 8 accounts. Can we agree Horizon will lead initial intro emails and Redwood will provide a templated outreach and content?
05:32 Jordan Patel: Yes. Horizon will lead intros; we'll use your email templates. We also want co-branded case studies and joint PR when we close a strategic deal.
05:43 Alex Chen: Makes sense. We can plan a marketing motion for two strategic closes in Q2.
05:48 Ethan Brooks: About competitive positioning: some prospects are already looking at Vertex AI deployed by their infra teams; we need to position Redwood as a production-ready inference layer with better cost controls and model routing.
06:03 Priya Nair: Agreed. Technical differentiators to highlight: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, KV cache and prefix caching to save tokens, intelligent batching, and smart routing for fallback. Also mention our rollouts and canary policy support.
06:28 Maya Gomez: Legal loops - SkyLine Systems is slow on contract. If they ask for custom indemnities or data processing addendums, what's Redwood's stance?
06:37 Alex Chen: We'll hand those to legal; typical timeline increases but we have standard DPAs and can support customer-specific addenda for enterprise. We'll get counsel involved early if they need unusual terms.
06:50 Jordan Patel: On the benchmarking front, can Priya run two configs: 1) hosted with baseline model and 2) dedicated with 8-GPU pool and quantized model, and give cost per 1k tokens and p95 latency?
07:06 Priya Nair: Yes, I'll do p95 latency, median throughput, and cost per 1k tokens for both. I need the customer's prompt set and sample traffic profile though.
07:16 Jordan Patel: I'll ask NovaBank for a sample prompt set and traffic numbers.
07:22 Alex Chen: Perfect. Also, for sales enablement, we should create a short battlecard addressing the typical objections: 'We need sub-200ms' (show dedicated layout), 'We won't store tokens' (show retention controls), 'We need EU data residency' (show region map).
07:40 Ethan Brooks: Any thoughts on incentives for Horizon reps? Could Redwood provide a small deal registration or margin protection?
07:47 Alex Chen: We can do deal registration via our partner portal and we can carve out co-sell margins in the pricing sheet. Also can discuss MDF for marketing if we hit commit thresholds.
07:59 Jordan Patel: Sounds good. For the joint deck, can you include two customer stories or reference architectures? Even if they're anonymized it's helpful.
08:07 Alex Chen: We have two anonymized case snapshots we'll add.
08:12 Maya Gomez: Quick question: for private deployments do we have SSO/SAML integration and RBAC? Horizon customers will ask.
08:20 Priya Nair: Yes, SSO/SAML and S C O R L - sorry transcription quirk - RBAC is supported with SCIM and SAML. We'll include the integration checklist.
08:35 Jordan Patel: Great. Any blockers from Redwood side to start the co-sell?
08:40 Alex Chen: Nothing major. We need to finalize partner pricing and the enablement pack. Also SE bandwidth for benchmarks — Priya, confirm ETA?
08:51 Priya Nair: I can start initial bench config this week; expect first draft results in two weeks, final by 2026-04-03.
09:02 Jordan Patel: Timeline fits. Next is exec intro — I'll gather times for week of 3/30.
09:09 Alex Chen: Okay. Let's recap actions and owners.
09:12 Alex Chen: Alex to send co-sell deck + partner pricing (due 3/22). Priya to run benchmarks and send configs + results (draft 3/31, final 4/03). Jordan to share prioritized list and sample prompts (due 3/24). Maya to provide security questionnaire items (due 3/27).
09:35 Maya Gomez: I'll also flag any customers that need EU data residency explicitly.
09:40 Ethan Brooks: One more - can Redwood provide a short checklist for POC environment requirements so Meridian's infra can prep?
09:47 Priya Nair: Yes, we'll send a POC runbook with infra checklist, sample adapter code for Kafka, and expected timelines.
10:01 Alex Chen: Perfect. We'll drop all artifacts into the shared drive: joint-pipeline-horizon.xlsx, co-sell-deck-v1.pdf, partner-pricing-anchors.xlsx, security-pack.zip. Links will be in the calendar invite follow up.
10:23 Jordan Patel: Awesome. Thanks everyone. That covers it from my side.
10:29 Alex Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the materials and schedule the exec intro.
10:34 Meeting ends.

Notes: transcript contains occasional time jitter in timestamps (typical of Fireflies exports). References to product names sometimes spaced out (e.g., V P C, K M S) due to ASR. Links referenced: shared drive joint pipeline spreadsheet (link: drive.google.com/drive/folders/partner-horizon), partner deck (link: drive.google.com/file/d/co-sell-deck-v1).
